input.quote: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
input.rationale: No audit right binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the Agreement, so there is nothing to limit and no edit is warranted. The sections that would ordinarily host a usage-verification right contain none: § 2 (grant, p0028), § 3 use restrictions (p0031-p0039, which impose only substantive use limits with no verification or reporting mechanism), § 14 (confidentiality), § 17 (term and termination) and § 20 general matters (p0134-p0147). Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "access", "premises", "remote", "report", "books" and "right to enter" return no audit, inspection, records-examination, monitoring or system-access right running against us. The two near-hits are not audit rights: p0114 is an examination/testing right over escrow materials held by Sparkling (in our favour), and p0118 is a one-time post-termination certification that Sparkling has ceased use, not a recurring audit or any access to our systems. Complete absence of an audit right is at least as favourable as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and proposing audit machinery would risk inviting a right that does not presently exist. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is a false signal: frequency-limiting language cannot be present where there is no audit clause to limit.
